title: A stair gate for children is not a pet gate, and the top step needs one that screws in
summary: CPSC says safety gates can block falls down stairs, pet gates should not be used for children, and the top of the stairs needs a gate that screws to the wall.
body: CPSC says safety gates help prevent falls down stairs and keep children out of rooms with other dangers. The gate should meet current child safety standards. Pet gates should never be used as a child gate. Older gates with a large V shape can trap a child's head and neck, and the page says to replace those. For the top of the stairs, it says to use only a gate that screws to the wall. A CDC page says most children walk up a few stairs by about two years. That timing is separate. This card is the gate itself. It is US product guidance, not a building code for every country.
